papers.summary: Spectral weight decay applies additive singular-value shrinkage. The authors report improved LLaMA compression at matched validation loss and better fixed-horizon clean-test accuracy under label noise than matched L2 regularization.
papers.relevance: Direct match for spectral regularization, low-rank compressibility, and noisy-label memorization.

evidence.quote: Across LLaMA models with 124 124 M to 500 500 M parameters, spectral weight decay improves low-rank compression and inference speed over standard weight decay at matched validation loss.
All coefficients are frozen before the five new label-corruption replications. Clean validation is not used to select checkpoints

papers.title: Spectral Weight Decay: Inducing Low-Rank Structure in Neural Network Weights

papers.summary: ORCA applies soft orthogonality regularization early, then removes it. In reported LLaMA pretraining runs, it lowers final validation loss relative to Muon at 350M and 1.3B parameters.
papers.relevance: Tests whether temporary spectral shaping improves training without imposing a persistent constraint.

evidence.quote: Compared with Muon, ORCA reduces the final loss by 0.0194 0.0194 at 350M and 0.0244 0.0244 at 1.3B
Then directly removes it at a single switch point. Training thereafter follows the standard optimizer update

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training

papers.summary: Derives singular-mode birth, saturation, and decay laws for several optimizers in deep matrix factorization under balance and alignment assumptions, with numerical tests in factorization and regression.
papers.relevance: Provides a framework for studying how optimizer geometry changes spectral bias and effective rank.

evidence.quote: Under explicit balance and alignment assumptions, we derive birth, saturation, and decay laws for Euclidean GD, coordinate-wise updates of SignGD and an instantaneous Adam approximation, spectral updates of Muon and cumulative Shampoo, and a block curvature model of K-FAC.
Controlled experiments in deep matrix factorization and regression verify the derived phase laws.

papers.title: Optimizer Geometry Sets the Pace: Spectral Learning Dynamics in Matrix Factorization

papers.summary: Relates low-rank LoRA solutions to the rank of the map through which frozen activations expose an adapted matrix. A restricted Qwen2.5-1.5B experiment tests the predicted rank threshold using training loss.
papers.relevance: Addresses why low-rank adaptation can suffice and how rank interacts with weight decay and frozen-feature geometry.

evidence.quote: This yields global minimizers whose ranks are controlled by the rank of this map, which we call the bottleneck rank , rather than the sample size.
Only one query-projection block in one head of layers 7 and 8 is adapted; after a classification-head warm-up, both the backbone and classifier are frozen.

papers.title: How Finite-Rank Bottlenecks Shape the Low-Rank Adaptation Landscape

papers.summary: Proposes geometry-aware LoRA preconditioning. On LLaMA2-7B commonsense tasks, the reported mean accuracy is 82.34 versus 81.68 for unpreconditioned AdamW LoRA.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimization of low-rank parameterizations and practical language-model fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: Table 3: Top-1 test accuracy in LoRA fine-tuning for the LLaMA2-7B model on the eight commonsense reasoning datasets with different preconditioning.

papers.title: A Riemannian Geometry for Low-rank Adaptation

papers.summary: PMRC retains projected momentum while correcting updates with the residual gradient. In 1.3B LLaMA pretraining it reports 2.570 validation loss and 53.44 GiB peak allocated memory; full-space Muon reports lower loss, 2.495, at 55.52 GiB.
papers.relevance: Makes the quality–memory tradeoff of low-rank optimizer states explicit across model scales.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon

papers.summary: Monarch–Muon combines structured weights with blockwise Muon updates. Its separate 6.89B systems benchmark reports lower peak memory and full-step time than dense Muon, while complete quality runs are at smaller scales.
papers.relevance: Especially useful for distinguishing optimizer-state savings from whole-training memory and throughput gains.

evidence.quote: At 6.89B, Monarch–Muon reduces the full-step time by 45% and peak memory by 23% relative to dense Muon.
The systems experiments measure training operations on larger reference architectures, separately from the complete quality runs in Appendix A.1 .

papers.title: Monarch-Muon: Structure-Aware Muon for Fast and Memory-Efficient Pretraining

papers.summary: ResQAdam preserves a sign-based update from momentum outside the principal low-rank subspace during quantization-aware training. On three reported LLMs, optimizer-state memory falls by 71.3%–73.2%, with 15.3%–19.5% less total peak memory and under 2% lower throughput than AdamW.
papers.relevance: Quantifies optimizer memory, peak memory, throughput, and quality tradeoffs in a specialized low-bit training setting.

evidence.quote: Opt. State Memory (GB) 7.78 / 2.16 ( ↓ \downarrow 72.2%) 10.48 / 3.01( ↓ \downarrow 71.3%) 29.07 / 7.78 ( ↓ \downarrow 73.2%) Total Peak Memory (GB) 33.33 / 28.24 ( ↓ \downarrow 15.3%) 43.93 / 37.19 ( ↓ \downarrow 15.3%) 99.14 / 79.77 ( ↓ \downarrow 19.5%)
The training throughput decreases by less than 2% compared to standard AdamW in all evaluated cases.

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

papers.summary: Idea2Prior records candidate identities, assessments, filtering decisions, and document evidence for idea-to-paper retrieval. Its historical 30-query comparison reports 16/30 target Hit@5, but the evaluation has disclosed protocol limitations.
papers.relevance: Directly informs auditable retrieval and relevance ranking in a research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: it preserves search queries, candidate identities, assessments, filtering reasons, PDF availability, and the final ranking.
The small, overlapping target set and historical protocol do not support a broad or statistically established superiority claim.

papers.title: Idea2Prior: Auditable Paper Retrieval and Ranking from Research Ideas

papers.summary: CORE searches broad passages but returns short reranked snippets, with source expansion and duplicate suppression in the harness. Reported closed-search comparisons show higher accuracy and evidence recall than two baseline harnesses across three agent models and benchmarks.
papers.relevance: Applicable to managing tool-output context in a handwritten research-agent harness.

evidence.quote: CORE searches at the passage level but returns evidence at the snippet level.
Across three agent models and three benchmarks, CORE achieves higher answer accuracy and evidence recall than Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher in every model–benchmark comparison

papers.title: CORE: Coarse-to-Fine Search with Context Management for Deep Research

limitations: Results are reported by the papers and have not been independently reproduced.
Some quoted HTML tables contain duplicated numbers or imperfect formatting; numeric comparisons were interpreted from the supplied passages.
The LoRA rank-threshold experiment adapts only a small part of Qwen2.5-1.5B, limiting conclusions about broader fine-tuning.
Monarch–Muon's largest-scale memory and timing results are systems measurements, not complete pretraining quality runs.
Idea2Prior's historical comparison includes overlapping targets, selected replacement runs, and a convention-based baseline credit.
CORE's evaluation uses closed search on fixed corpora, not this digest's paper corpus.
X analysis was disabled; no attention or popularity claim is made.
